W.note: A cream face with a lilac halo that fades in over a 650 ms tail reads most like light in a dark room, with real custom curves (220 ms in, 300 ms out, a rebound option) and a reduced-motion path, though the tuning console makes it feel like a prototype and the hover crops never caught the focal button.

X.note: It has the most dreamlike effects (aura, sheen, motes), but overflow hidden clips the aura, the white label sits on the light sky stop of the gradient, the motes loop while hovered, and the hover crops cut the button off, so it reads as a candy gradient more than ethereal.

Y.note: A slate face with a blurred under-glow and a lilac fill fade is clean, legible and cheap to render, with a documented curve panel, a focus ring and a reduced-motion path, though the fill uses a plain ease-out and the hover reads as a tint more than a dream.

Z.note: The card has a sensible focus ring and removes movement under reduced motion, but the shimmer pseudo-element sits outside the button at rest and shows as a white smudge on the page, letter-spacing animates (a layout cost), and the look is a standard gradient SaaS button.
